items.note: Same fact as existing nb:safe-01 (PPE donning sequence gown-mask-goggles-gloves). Rewritten as the sequence for putting on and seal-checking a disposable N95 respirator (CDC/NIOSH); same id, labels and type.

Near-duplicate of existing nb:nb-integ-04 (client on chemotherapy with zoster on multiple dermatomes: airborne + contact). Rewritten as precautions for norovirus in an incontinent client (CDC 2007 Appendix A: contact precautions for incontinent/diapered clients and outbreaks); same id, labels and key position.

The keyed return-to-work rule ("fever-free 24 hours") is no longer the full CDC criterion: CDC's healthcare-personnel guidance for viral respiratory infections (updated 2025-2026) adds at least 3 days from symptom onset and improving symptoms. Since the criteria recently changed, the key now tests the stable concept (stay home and follow employee health return criteria) without numbers.

Near-verbatim duplicate of existing nb:nb26-infx-024 (C. difficile room disinfection with a sporicidal product). Rewritten as preparing a client on contact precautions for transport (CDC 2007: cover/contain the site, remove used PPE before transport); same id, labels and key position.

Same facts as existing nb:u2-safe-002 and nb:nb26-infx-038 (needlestick first aid and reporting). Rewritten as respiratory hygiene/cough etiquette measures in an outpatient waiting room (CDC 2007 standard precautions element); same id, labels and type.

Same fact as existing nb:nb26-core-006 (banana/avocado/kiwi cross-reactivity with latex). Rewritten as recognizing the highest-risk client for latex allergy (spina bifida with repeated surgeries and catheterization); same id, labels and key position.

Same facts as existing nb:nb26-sabc-005 (no two-handed recapping, activate safety device, point-of-use disposal, three-quarters-full container). Rewritten as evaluating a protective environment for an allogeneic stem cell transplant client (CDC 2007: no fresh or dried flowers or potted plants); same id, labels and key position.
cjmm label was prioritizeHypotheses, but the item sequences actions once TB is already suspected; relabeled takeAction.

Rationale for perinatal transmission said it is prevented by "newborn vaccine and immune globulin" generally; the CDC hepatitis B birth-dose recommendation for infants of HBsAg-negative mothers changed in 2025-2026, so the rationale now refers only to the stable recommendation for infants of mothers with hepatitis B. Takeaway reworded to testing and offering vaccine to susceptible contacts.

Rationale said influenza vaccine is recommended "for everyone 6 months and older"; CDC moved pediatric influenza vaccination to shared clinical decision-making in January 2026 (disputed by AAP), so wording now refers to adults only. Takeaway implied a complete list for age 50+, although pneumococcal (lowered to 50 in 2024) and hepatitis B (19-59) are also on the adult schedule; reworded so it does not claim completeness. Key unchanged and verified against the current CDC adult schedule (RZV at 50+, Td/Tdap every 10 years, LAIV only through 49, HPV not recommended after 45).

Rationale and takeaway said influenza vaccine is recommended "for everyone 6 months and older"; CDC moved pediatric influenza vaccination to shared clinical decision-making in January 2026 (disputed), so wording now refers to adults, which is unchanged and is what the item tests.
Keyed option was much longer than the distractors (length cue). Shortened the key and lengthened the distractors to similar length.

Same fact as existing nb:nb26-repr-003 (rifampin reduces combined oral contraceptive effectiveness; use a nonhormonal method). Rewritten as dolutegravir-antacid spacing (DailyMed: 2 hours before or 6 hours after polyvalent-cation antacids); same id, labels and key position.

Same fact as existing rnr:renal-019 (tacrolimus teaching: avoid grapefruit). Rewritten as verifying a negative HLA-B*5701 result before abacavir (DailyMed boxed warning); same id, labels and key position.

Same item as existing rnr:shock-042 (epinephrine auto-injector teaching SATA); its "call emergency services after every use" key is also no longer absolute under the 2023 AAAAI/ACAAI anaphylaxis practice parameter. Rewritten as IV immune globulin administration (DailyMed boxed warning: hydration, slow rate, monitoring); same id, labels and type.

Same fact as existing nb:nb-resp-06 (BCG-vaccinated employee: IGRA preferred). Rewritten as the recommended initial laboratory HIV screening test (HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody combination immunoassay); same id, labels and key position.

Rationale said clients are "observed for several hours"; the 2023 anaphylaxis practice parameter allows a shorter observation for prompt, complete responders and extended observation for severe reactions. Reworded so the key rests on the undisputed point (30 minutes is too soon to go home; biphasic reactions occur).

Same item as existing rnr:shock-026 (septic shock reassessment matrix: MAP 70, urine output, mottling, lactate, mental status). Rewritten as evaluating response to treatment for Pneumocystis pneumonia; same id, labels and type.
Keyed option was much longer than the distractors (length cue). Shortened the key and lengthened the distractors to similar length and detail.
